children.text: Three absolute electrical measurements are considered. Use vacuum permeability \(\mu_0\). In the Kelvin method, a closed \(N\)-turn circular coil of radius \(a\) and resistance \(R\) rotates at angular speed \(\omega\) about its vertical diameter in a horizontal field \(B_0\). Its inductance is negligible. At \(t=0\) its normal points along \(B_0\). A slowly responding magnetic needle at its centre measures the time-averaged field. In the Lorenz method, two conducting discs of radius \(b\) share a shaft rotating at \(\omega\). Each is centred in an \(N\)-turn coil of radius \(a\gg b\), carrying opposite currents \(I\). The coils are far apart. Brushes and a null galvanometer connect the disc rims as shown. Finally, an Ampere balance uses six single-turn coils of radius \(a\), in series. On each side of the balance, a moving coil is midway between two fixed coils at distances \(h\ll a\). Currents give a net upward force on coil 2 and downward force on coil 5. The equal arm lengths are \(d\). A mass \(m\) at horizontal distance \(x\) balances the electromagnetic torque. Ignore interactions between opposite sides and approximate neighbouring wire segments as straight.

statement.text:
Absolute measurements of electrical quantities
Three absolute electrical measurements are considered. Use vacuum permeability \(\mu_0\). In the Kelvin method, a closed \(N\)-turn circular coil of radius \(a\) and resistance \(R\) rotates at angular speed \(\omega\) about its vertical diameter in a horizontal field \(B_0\). Its inductance is negligible. At \(t=0\) its normal points along \(B_0\). A slowly responding magnetic needle at its centre measures the time-averaged field. In the Lorenz method, two conducting discs of radius \(b\) share a shaft rotating at \(\omega\). Each is centred in an \(N\)-turn coil of radius \(a\gg b\), carrying opposite currents \(I\). The coils are far apart. Brushes and a null galvanometer connect the disc rims as shown. Finally, an Ampere balance uses six single-turn coils of radius \(a\), in series. On each side of the balance, a moving coil is midway between two fixed coils at distances \(h\ll a\). Currents give a net upward force on coil 2 and downward force on coil 5. The equal arm lengths are \(d\). A mass \(m\) at horizontal distance \(x\) balances the electromagnetic torque. Ignore interactions between opposite sides and approximate neighbouring wire segments as straight.

1.emf. Induced emf
Find the emf as a function of time.
1.power. Average power
Find the average dissipated power.
2. Kelvin resistance
The needle deflects by a small angle \(\theta\) relative to \(B_0\). Determine \(R\).
3. Two-disc emf

Find the total emf between rims 1 and 4.
4. Lorenz resistance
Find the resistance measured when the galvanometer reads zero.
5. Force between neighbouring coils

Find the force magnitude between coils 1 and 2.
6. Current from balance
Determine the current in terms of the balance parameters.
7. Restoring displacement
The balance has mass \(M\) and its centre of gravity is a distance \(l\) below the pivot, excluding the suspended coils and added mass. Find the largest small upward displacement \(\delta z\) of coil 2, with coil 5 moving down, for which the balance remains restoring. Use \(\delta z\ll h\), small angles, and expand \((1\pm u)^{-1}\simeq1\mp u+u^2\).

children.text: Faraday's law applied to \(N\pi a^2B_0\cos\omega t\) gives \[\mathcal E=N\pi a^2B_0\omega\sin\omega t.\]
With negligible inductance, \(i=\mathcal E/R\), and the mean of \(\sin^2\) is \(1/2\). Thus \(\overline P=(N\pi a^2B_0\omega)^2/(2R)\).

The rotating current produces an average transverse field \(\overline B_y=\mu_0N^2\pi aB_0\omega/(4R)\), and zero mean parallel field. Therefore \[R=\frac{\mu_0N^2\pi a\omega}{4\tan\theta}\simeq\frac{\mu_0N^2\pi a\omega}{4\theta}.\]
Each coil produces \(B=\mu_0NI/(2a)\). Radial integration of \(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B\) gives \(B\omega b^2/2\) per disc. The two contributions add: \[\mathcal E=\mu_0Nb^2\omega I/(2a).\]
The force per unit length between parallel wires is \(\mu_0I^2/(2\pi h)\). Multiply by \(2\pi a\) to get \(F=\mu_0aI^2/h\).
Four equal force contributions give \(mgx=4Fd\). Thus \[I=\sqrt{\frac{mghx}{4\mu_0ad}}.\]

The gravitational restoring torque is \(Mgl\sin\delta\phi+mgx\cos\delta\phi\). The magnetic torque is \(2\mu_0aI^2d[1/(h-\delta z)+1/(h+\delta z)]\cos\delta\phi\). Use \(\delta\phi\simeq\delta z/d\), cancel the equilibrium torque and keep the leading displacement terms. The restoring condition on the specified side is \[0<\delta z<\frac{Mlh^2}{mxd}.\] The upper bound is a small-displacement estimate and is valid only if it is much smaller than \(h\).

solution.text:
Absolute measurements of electrical quantities
1.emf. Induced emf
Faraday's law applied to \(N\pi a^2B_0\cos\omega t\) gives \[\mathcal E=N\pi a^2B_0\omega\sin\omega t.\]
1.power. Average power
With negligible inductance, \(i=\mathcal E/R\), and the mean of \(\sin^2\) is \(1/2\). Thus \(\overline P=(N\pi a^2B_0\omega)^2/(2R)\).
2. Kelvin resistance
The rotating current produces an average transverse field \(\overline B_y=\mu_0N^2\pi aB_0\omega/(4R)\), and zero mean parallel field. Therefore \[R=\frac{\mu_0N^2\pi a\omega}{4\tan\theta}\simeq\frac{\mu_0N^2\pi a\omega}{4\theta}.\]
3. Two-disc emf
Each coil produces \(B=\mu_0NI/(2a)\). Radial integration of \(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B\) gives \(B\omega b^2/2\) per disc. The two contributions add: \[\mathcal E=\mu_0Nb^2\omega I/(2a).\]
4. Lorenz resistance
At null, \(IR=\mathcal E\), so \(R=\mu_0Nb^2\omega/(2a)\).
5. Force between neighbouring coils
The force per unit length between parallel wires is \(\mu_0I^2/(2\pi h)\). Multiply by \(2\pi a\) to get \(F=\mu_0aI^2/h\).
6. Current from balance
Four equal force contributions give \(mgx=4Fd\). Thus \[I=\sqrt{\frac{mghx}{4\mu_0ad}}.\]
7. Restoring displacement
The gravitational restoring torque is \(Mgl\sin\delta\phi+mgx\cos\delta\phi\). The magnetic torque is \(2\mu_0aI^2d[1/(h-\delta z)+1/(h+\delta z)]\cos\delta\phi\). Use \(\delta\phi\simeq\delta z/d\), cancel the equilibrium torque and keep the leading displacement terms. The restoring condition on the specified side is \[0<\delta z<\frac{Mlh^2}{mxd}.\] The upper bound is a small-displacement estimate and is valid only if it is much smaller than \(h\).
